The main takeaway from our work is that

G-CSF prophlylaxis is now recommended to support the use of dose-dense and/or dose-intense regimens, and to maintain dose density where chemotherapy dose reductions have been associated with compromised outcomes.

, with the availability of a range of new and more effective agents, there is now an urgent need to re-evaluate the use of G-CSF in the context of the overall management of cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
